title: Keep the existing R3F world post-processing pipeline stable across quality changes

scope.subject: Remove avoidable EffectComposer and PlanetPass reconstruction during ordinary quality changes while preserving HIGH visuals and software fallback behavior

research_summary: The current CinematicPipeline already uses the project-standard React Three Fiber Canvas, Three.js EffectComposer and ProceduralPlanets PlanetPass, but quality is included in the composer memo dependencies. AUTO -> LOW -> AUTO therefore reconstructs the post-processing graph even when the renderer, scene and camera are unchanged. Reuse the existing framework-owned renderer and retain one GPU composer/pass graph on hardware paths, toggling pass enablement and mutable bloom parameters instead of rebuilding it. Keep the software-renderer exception bounded: AUTO/LOW should not allocate PlanetPass under SwiftShader, while HIGH may still construct the live PlanetPass because HIGH explicitly preserves intended live visuals.

sources.finding: React Three Fiber exposes the stable renderer, scene and camera through useThree and drives frame work through useFrame, so post-processing should remain attached to that single renderer rather than create another rendering authority.
Three.js EffectComposer owns an ordered pass chain with explicit setSize, setPixelRatio, render and dispose lifecycle methods; the existing composer can be retained while pass properties change.

ProceduralPlanets is already the selected live-world subsystem and its PlanetPass is part of the existing post-processing chain, so reuse its enable/disable lifecycle instead of replacing the planet renderer.

search_ladder.conclusion: This is a bounded hot-path and resource-lifetime correction inside the selected rendering stack, not a replacement application or renderer.
Keep the R3F-owned WebGLRenderer and one EffectComposer attached to its stable scene/camera instead of rebuilding the graph for every quality value.
Retain the existing ProceduralPlanets PlanetPass as the live-world subsystem and switch its enabled state according to product quality/fallback decisions.
No additional post-processing or GPU resource component is needed because the existing EffectComposer and PlanetPass already expose the required lifecycle.

candidates.name: Retain one R3F-owned EffectComposer graph per renderer/scene/camera
candidates.source: Existing R3F Canvas plus Three.js EffectComposer lifecycle
candidates.reason: This keeps the current single renderer authority and removes avoidable GPU target/pass reconstruction without changing product navigation or renderer ownership.

candidates.name: Retain ProceduralPlanets PlanetPass and toggle enablement on supported hardware
candidates.reason: The selected live-world subsystem already supplies the correct planet render pass; retaining it on hardware paths avoids shader/program churn while LOW and software AUTO can keep it disabled.

candidates.name: Build a project-owned composer/pass cache and GPU resource pool
candidates.reason: A second resource manager would duplicate R3F, Three.js and ProceduralPlanets ownership, increase teardown complexity and solve a problem already addressed by retaining the existing objects.

decision.rationale: Reuse the existing R3F renderer and ProceduralPlanets pass graph. On hardware WebGL, allocate the composer and PlanetPass once for a stable renderer/scene/camera, then mutate enablement and bloom parameters as quality changes. On software WebGL, keep AUTO/LOW lightweight and only allocate PlanetPass for explicit HIGH. This removes ordinary quality-switch reconstruction without weakening HIGH or creating a second renderer/resource authority.
decision.fallback: If retained PlanetPass on a real GPU proves to hold excessive idle resources, keep the stable composer but allow only the PlanetPass itself to be lazily created for a close-world live phase; do not recreate the whole composer on every quality change.
